svg.title: A window separates a visible exterior from a private interior.

text.tspan: A window separates a visible exterior from a private interior.
A wonderful fact to reflect
upon, that every human
creature is constituted to be
that profound secret and
mystery to every other.
The narrator · Charles Dickens · A Tale of Two Cities, Book I, Chapter III ·
Published 1859
At the opening of The Night Shadows, Dickens
pauses the journey to consider how little people can
know of one another. The narrator imagines a city
filled with houses, rooms and private thoughts. Even
the person nearest to someone cannot enter every
part of that person's inner life. The passage deepens
the novel's atmosphere of secrecy. It also turns an
ordinary encounter between travellers into a
reflection on the limits of human understanding.
Constituted to be means formed or made in such a
way. Profound intensifies the mystery: the narrator is
considering inner experience, not merely information
that could be obtained by asking a few more
questions.
How does the image of houses containing rooms
help the narrator express the idea of private thought?
